You seem like a racing game aficionado: I've only played racing games against the AI. Am I missing out?

I wouldn't say so, really. There are some games where you're made very aware whether you're competing against AI or humans, but Forza isn't really one of those in my opinion. The campaign is usually pretty long, the AI drivers are effective, and Forza has a "drivatar" system where it will learn your friends' driving style and implement it in your campaign as a dedicated AI driver. You don't miss as much from skipping the multiplayer as you would in other games.

Forza has a "drivatar" system where it will learn your friends' driving style and implement it in your campaign as a dedicated AI driver.

Holy shit. The future is here.

I thought the same thing when I started playing it! And honestly it's a pretty neat feature. I tend to be aggressive and shoulder people to the outside when I turn, so that's how my drivatar plays. My brother outpaces me on straighaways but is less effecient around corners, so that's how his drivatar plays. Drivatar data carries across Forza releases, so I've been training mine for the past few Forza games just by playing. They added a setting in Forza Motorsport 6 where you can dial back aggression on drivatars if you need to, in case you have too many friends that go for the throat when cornering.

It's a feature I'd love to see implemented in other games, like Super Smash Bros or Mario Kart. I hope the feature makes it into the PC version of Forza 6. It makes single-player a lot more fun, and it's a great way to feel connected to my friends even when they're not online.

If you enjoy racing against AI then Drivatars brings an interesting gimmick to how AI act and react. I personally like to do drift tandems with friends. Drivatars only really understand how to circuit race. So what my drivatar learns is: to gun it in the corners, take a terrible line in turns, and roll slowly in straights. This makes it very aggressive and unpleasant to drive against.

Another thing that I like to organize are rolling drag races or just drag races on tracks.

Neither of these things are meant to see who finishes however many laps first but just to goof around and have fun. These "events" usually have us going in reverse or turning around before we complete a full lap. Without multiplayer, me and my friends can't do either.

Forza is one of my favorite Xbox franchises. I'm happy it's coming to PC, but I don't like the "Forza Lite" treatment it's potentially getting; I'd much rather see a completely faithful port of Forza Motorsport 6.
Forza has great graphics, but imagine what they could be if they took advantage of the power PC has to offer instead of using it as Xbox advertising.
Very true. And to me it's one of those franchises that's too fun to be locked down to one platform.
